caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 117 of 1995.
lawyer:
Sirajul Hoque Senior Advocate, instructed by Mvi. Md. Wahidullah Advocate-on-Record — For the Petitioner.
 Abu Salek, Advocate, instructed by Md. Aftab Hossain Advocate-on-Record — For Respondent No. 1 
Respondent No. 2 — Not represented.
parties:
Anwarul Haque ----- Petitioner.
vs.
Md. Shahidul Islam and another ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Md. Ismailuddin Sarker J: The accused petitioner has filed this petition for leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated May 7, 1995 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division discharging the Rule issued earlier in Criminal Revision No. 1035 under section 561 A of 1993 of the Code of Criminal Procedure praying for quashing the proceedings of CR case No. 498 of 1993 pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong. 

 2. One Shahidul Islam, former Director of Sapid Seas Ltd, filed a petition of complaint before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong on August 19, 1990 alleging, inter alia, that by a deed of agreement between him and the accused petitioner, he transferred his entire share numbering 4100 held in the Sapid Seas Company Limited in favour of the petitioner for a consideration of Taka 4,00.000 only and on that date the petitioner paid Taka 1,00.000 by a pay order and issued a post-dated cheque for Taka 3,00.000 to be encashed on November 3, 1990. But when the complainant presented the said cheque through his Current Account No. 193 with Agrani Bank, Lalkhan Bazar Branch, Chittagong the cheque was dishonoured three times on January 1, 1991, March 24, 1991 and June 6, 1991. Thereafter the complainant demanded the money from the accused-petitioner on several occasions but every time the petitioner made false promises and ultimately denied the transaction on April 25, 1993 and turned the complainant away in presence of witnesses. The Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong examined the complainant on May 4, 1993 and took cognizance of the offence under sections 420/406 of the Penal Code against the accused petitioner and directed to issue process. The accused petitioner was arrested on June 7, 1993 and released on bail on June 8, 1993 by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong. Thereafter the accused petitioner filed an application under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure in the High Court Division and obtained the above Rule on May 7, 1995 and the said Rule was heard by a Division Bench of the High Court Division who by the impugned judgment discharged the Rule on the ground that the case was a premature one as section 241 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure had not been complied with. 

 3. It appears from the impugned judgment that the learned judges of the High Court Division have not considered the facts of the case but upon making reference to amendments brought about in Chapters XXIII and XX of the Code of Criminal Procedure by the Law Reforms Ordinance, 1978 took the view that an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure will be premature unless the accused-petitioner had gone through the stages under section 265C or 241 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and accordingly discharged the Rule, not on merit but as premature one observing, that the accused petitioner may file an application under section 241A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, if so advised. 

 4. This Division after making reference to the Privy Council case of Emperor vs Nazir Ahmed, AIR 1945 (PC) 18, the case of Abdul Quarter Chowdhury vs State 28 DLR (AD) 39 and the case of Nasiruddin Mahmud vs. Momtazuddin Ahmed 36 DLR (AD) 14, in the case of Syed Mohamad Hashem vs. State, 1995 BLD (AD) 115, observed that the aforesaid view expressed by the High Court Division was not consistent with the principles as already settled and, referred to the above mentioned cases and it would have been easier for the High Court Division to dismiss the petition on merit instead of laying down a new principle. 

 5. Mr. Sirajul Haque, learned Counsel for the accused petitioner submitted that the learned judges of the High Court Division caused a miscarriage of justice by not considering the facts and circumstances of the present case on an erroneous view of law though it had the power under section 561A CrPC to quash the proceeding to prevent the abuse of the process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice. 

 6. In the instant case we have perused the petition of complaint and it cannot be said that prima facie the allegations made therein do not constitute an offence. That being the position we are satisfied that no interference is called for on the merit of the case and as such the petition is dismissed.
